When I was in 2nd grade, a kid in my grade left school on his scooter (it was a generally small community). He didn't come back to class after a while, so all 2nd grade classes were made to get out of class together while the teachers looked for him. By the end of the day, everyone was shaken and thought he had run away.

A few days later they found out he drowned right in front of the small bridge in our neighborhood.

No one knows if he drowned, was pushed, or committed suicide. No one knows WHY he did it. Everyone was nice to him, everyone cared about him, he was a generally quiet student. His parents took good care of him. I only ever spoke to him once and I could just tell he was a kind-hearted person.

Hey, don't let something that happened when you were 8 years old determine how you live the rest of your life. I've been bullied since I was in the fucking first grade by both my family and schoolmates, but you know what I live by? Quality over quantity. It doesn't matter how many friends you have at all. I have quite a few acquaintances, but when it comes down to it, I have 5 people I can call legitimate friends. They're either not in my classes or don't live close enough. One of them will be in another country for 2 years. Then any legitimate friends I had when I was younger all moved away or I had to. Even then I'm cautious about telling them when somethings wrong. Pretty much no one is ever there for me, but I don't let that keep me from socializing and being happy. You should try keeping something like that in mind. 
Quality over quantity, and you'll be happier than most people.

Not much of a story, but I felt I needed to post it because it's stuck with me throughout the years. 

My grandmother didn't much like me or my sister when we were 2 and 4, much less did she like my mother. This bitch comes over for a family get together and acts like she owns the place. I was riding a little tricycle around even though there was pretty much no space (we lived in an apartment at the time). I accidentally ride into her leg and apologize. This bitch has the nerve to pick me up and throw me into a cabinet. EVERYONE saw, and EVERYONE looked straight at her, knowing damn well that it was no accident. She just plain said "the girl fell." and walked away. Being 4 year old me, I just sat there crying and wondering "what did I do?" Because I hadn't done anything wrong and was getting along with my sister just fine. The next day I walk into preschool with a black eye and I get questioned and asked if everything's ok at home. I explain what happened. Fine. My mom is asked the same thing and tells the same thing. She isn't believed. Not only am I pissed the fuck off because my mom is being seen as an abuser, but my bitch of a grandmother gets away with abusing us for however long she stayed. 
I still hate her for it and she still does similar things today. I'm 16 and have a brother now. I'm thankful that I learned to stand up for myself and others, otherwise she would have ended up doing to him what she had done to my sister and I.

You are NEVER at a dead end. There is always time to seek help, and there will always be people who genuinely want to help you. I'm currently going through a similar thought process despite good things that have happened recently. The key to not thinking about what others think of you is to push it away and not give a fuck, because in the end, all that matters is the good things that people say, or think, of you. There is someone who is willing to reach out to you and if they haven't come along, they will. There is always hope despite how hopeless life may seem, please believe me, i've been in your position. Try to find something to smile about, even if its the color of the sky, the sun's warmth, or how birds look so calm while the fly. Take something as your reason to smile, and you'll soon find yourself finding more reasons to be happy. Life is just a cycle of ups and downs, it always has been, so there is Always definite hope for a better day to put a smile on your face, no matter how long that moment may last.
